summary: On the pinned 20x20 fixup rig both sides render the same Christmas scene with a byte-identical tree silhouette, star column and ground band, but the port is wrong on all three of the remaining axes: its snowflakes are 2x2-aligned blocks that sit still for a median 6.5 s (original: 1-px antialiased points drifting right at ~0.75 px/s with a median 2.0 s dwell), giving ~2.7x the standing snow coverage; its tree decorations span the whole hue wheel in 2-px pairs instead of the original's red-plus-blue long garland stripes; and its whole palette is 30-45% darker with a 5-row star instead of 4.
observations: FIXUP RIG CONFIRMED. meta.json provenance.fixups.rig = {grid:[20,20]} on every run; the rig reported is 'grid, 400px, 20x20' and BOTH sides compile and render with compileError null / runtimeError null. Baseline (6 s, 20 fps): orig meanBrightness 90.8 [88-92], port 74.7 [71-76]; both brightnessTrend 'steady'. The prior re-judge blocker (original erroring at frame 0) is gone on this rig.

The original's pixel-count constraint is still real and still one-sided: --rig strip --pixels 64 gives orig 'RUNTIME ERR @0: array index out of bounds' while the port renders fine (mean 68); --pixels 300 (a multiple of 20) renders on both. So the port does not replicate the original's 20-multiple requirement — a behavioural difference the fixup rig hides, worth deciding on deliberately.

RIG MAPPING IS SHARED. At t=0 the flat pixel sequence of grid 20x20 is byte-identical to strip 400 on BOTH sides (0/400 differing pixels each). Reshaping to grid 40x10 changes the output by a near-identical amount on both sides (orig 161/400, port 159/400 at t=0; 161 vs 168 at t=3), so both patterns key off the rig width the same way. Not a port bug.

SCENE GEOMETRY MATCHES EXACTLY at t=0 on 20x20. Both draw the same stepped triangle: row1 cols 9-10, rows 4-5 cols 7&12, row6 cols 6-13, rows 7-9 cols 4-15, rows 10-12 cols 2-17, row13 cols 1-18, rows 14-16 cols 0-19, with a solid 3-row ground band on rows 17-19 (exactly 60 px on both sides) and the star centred on cols 8-11.

STAR HEIGHT MISMATCH. Original star = 16 px (rows 2-5 x cols 8-11) at [255,235,61]; port star = 20 px (rows 2-6 x cols 8-11) at [255,215,76]. Confirmed by exact colour counts at t=0, 3.7, 11.3, 19.1 and 27.3 s (orig 16 every time, port 20 every time). Star hue: orig 53.7 deg, port 46.6 deg.

BASE PALETTE, exact RGB at t=0 (orig vs port). Sky [57,60,142] x150 vs [26,44,89] x147 — port is 0.54x the brightness and its hue moves from indigo 238 deg to azure 223 deg. Ground/trunk [107,51,10] x60 vs [63,34,12] x60 — same hue (25 deg) at 0.59x brightness. Tree green [40,203,0] x126 vs [4,203,0] x114 — same value, but the ORIGINAL's green is exactly the sweep's signature 51,255,0 scaled by 0.796 (hue 108 deg) while the port sits at hue 119 deg. Silver tinsel [152,149,122] x26 vs [127,116,89] x24 — port dimmer and warmer (hue 54/sat 0.20 vs hue 43/sat 0.30). Neither side uses the template's neutral 114,114,114.

DECORATION HUE FAMILIES DIVERGE (measured at t=0, non-base pixels outside the star box; ornament colours are STATIC on both sides — byte-identical at t=0, 3.7, 11.3, 19.1, 27.3 s). Original: 48 decoration px = 26 low-sat silver (hue 54, sat 0.20) plus saturated runs confined to just two hue zones — red/orange at 359-20 deg (row7 cols5-7 ramping h9,15,20; row14 cols6-10 ramping h359,4,9,14,19) and blue at 240-261 deg (row9 cols11-15 h241..261; row16 cols14-18 h240..261) — plus a single stray green pixel at h138. Port: 59 decoration px = 24 silver plus saturated pairs spread over FIVE hue families — orange/red h12-36, green h107-127, cyan/azure h194-218, violet h285-305, azure h202-223. No magenta, cyan or green garland ever appears on the original in 30 frames sampled across 240 s.

GARLAND LAYOUT DIVERGES. Original silver runs are LONG horizontal stripes: 9 px (row8 cols5-13), 4 px (row12 cols3-6), 10 px (row13 cols7-16), 3 px (row14 cols17-19); its saturated runs are 3 and 5 px hue ramps. Port draws the same total budget as SHORT pieces: every saturated ornament is exactly a 2-px pair (two-step hue ramp) and its silver runs are 3-5 px, scattered over rows 6-16. Visually the original reads as tinsel stripes, the port as rainbow confetti.

SNOW GEOMETRY — the biggest structural defect. Measured over 120 dumps 0.5 s apart on a 62 s / 20 fps run, classifying a pixel as snow when it differs from its own modal colour: original horizontal run-length histogram {1:114, 2:110, 3:30, 4:3}, mean run 1.70 px, max 4; port {1:73, 2:85, 3:82, 4:49, 5:30, 6:26, 7:7, 8:17, 9:9, 11:4, 14:1}, mean 3.43 px, max 14. Vertical adjacency: only 10% of the original's snow pixels have a snow pixel directly above/below, versus 54% of the port's.

THE PORT QUANTISES SNOW TO A 2x2 LATTICE. Vertical snow pairs on the port start on an EVEN row 635 times vs 152 on an odd row (4.2:1), and its 2-px horizontal runs start on an EVEN column 422 times vs 69 odd (6.1:1). The original shows no parity preference at all (vertical pairs 11 even / 20 odd out of 1293 lit px; 2-px run starts 181 even / 164 odd). So the port renders each flake as a 2x2 block snapped to even coordinates, while the original renders a 1-px point with true sub-pixel antialiasing (its transits show split values like 112/255 then 31/255 across two adjacent columns).

SNOW PERSISTENCE ~3x TOO LONG. Per-pixel snow dwell over the 62 s / 20 fps window: orig median 2.00 s, mean 1.87 s, max 4.5 s (modal bucket 2.0 s); port median 6.50 s, mean 5.92 s, max 14.0 s (modal bucket 7.0 s). Onset rates are comparable (orig 5.77 pixel-onsets/s, port 4.98), so the excess coverage is entirely dwell, not spawn rate.

SNOW COVERAGE ~2.7x. Average snow-affected pixels per frame: orig 10.8/400, port 29.5/400. Sampled every 7.9 s across 240 s the original holds 8-24 px (mean 14.5) while the port ranges 7-75 px (mean 43.8); the port's t=0.3 value is 7 and it settles into a noisy 29-75 band by ~30 s with no further trend, so this is a higher, noisier steady state rather than a runaway.

SNOW MOTION DIVERGES — the port's flakes barely drift. Circular cross-correlation of the snow residual field between dumps (40 dumps 0.3 s apart, 20 fps): the ORIGINAL peaks at lag +1 px at dt=1.2 s (score 23.4 at +1 vs 0.3 at -1) and +2 px at dt=3.0 s, i.e. a coherent rightward drift of ~0.67-0.83 px/s, decorrelating by dt=6 s (flake lifetime). The PORT is pinned at lag 0 for dt=0.3/0.6/1.2/3.0 s with a near-symmetric lag profile (dt=1.2 s: -1 scores 28.4 vs +1 26.2), i.e. no net translation; it only shows a weak +1 preference at dt=6 s once correlation has already collapsed. Row traces confirm the mechanism: the original's flake steps one column every ~1.1 s and vacates the one behind (row1 col12 at 0.3 s -> col13 0.6 -> col14 1.2 -> col15 2.4 -> col16 3.6 -> col17 5.1), whereas the port's blocks advance rightward at a similar rate but do NOT extinguish behind, so a single flake smears into a bar (row2 cols 6-7 held at 255 continuously from 3.6 s to 9.3 s while cols 3,4,5 lit and faded around it).

SNOW COLOUR SCHEME ACTUALLY MATCHES in structure. Both sides use TWO warm tones split by what is behind the flake: over the sky orig [255,244,153] (87 px-frames on sky, 0 on tree) vs port [255,232,153] (420 sky / 0 tree); over the tree orig [255,235,63] (93 tree / 1 sky) vs port [255,194,38] (409 tree / 42 sky). Only the hues differ slightly (orig 53.5/53.7 deg, port 46.5/43.1 deg) and the port's tree tone is more saturated (0.85 vs 0.75). Both sides also fade flakes through dim values ([55,52,33], [81,77,48], [26,24,6] on the original; [31,28,18], [88,80,52], [56,51,34] on the port) so flakes read as dark specks at the extremes on both.

NO MODE/REGIME STRUCTURE ON EITHER SIDE. The 240 s / 5 fps survey rhythm images show a single continuous regime: the original's is a steady blue/green column field with fine rightward diagonal streaks (the drifting flakes); the port's is the same column field with coarser, blotchier warm patches and no boundaries. The 12-cell survey sheets at 0/21.8/43.6/.../239.8 s show the same scene at every sample on both sides. No banding, no cycle, nothing to park a --skip inside beyond the steady-state check.

STEADY STATE: BOTH ALIVE, PORT PERSISTENTLY DIMMER. Over 240 s at 5 fps: orig meanBrightness 88.8 [87-91], meanR [77-84], motion avg 1.1, zeroMotionFrames 55/1200; port meanBrightness 81.5 [71-98], meanR [52-101], motion avg 0.6, zeroMotionFrames 508/1200. A late window (--skip 200, 20 s at 20 fps) gives orig 90.1 [89-92] / port 75.9 [72-79], both 'steady' — neither side dies, freezes or blacks out. The port's much higher zero-motion count (42% vs 5% of frames) is the direct consequence of its long-lived static blocks; its much wider meanR swing (49 counts vs 7) is the consequence of the fluctuating block population.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING IS NOT A DIVERGENCE. Snow dwell measured identically at 10/20/40 fps: orig median 2.50 / 2.00 / 1.50 s (mean 2.58 / 1.87 / 1.30), port 10.50 / 6.50 / 4.00 s (mean 8.94 / 5.92 / 3.61). Both sides shorten dwell as fps rises, by a similar factor (orig 1.7-2.0x from 10 to 40 fps, port 2.5-2.6x), and neither is fps-invariant nor cleanly frame-counted — it is a shared hybrid. The port's ~3x dwell excess holds at every rate (4.2x at 10 fps, 3.25x at 20, 2.7x at 40), so the defect is not a frame-rate artefact.

SEED-INDEPENDENT. 60 s / 5 fps at seeds 1, 7 and 1234: orig meanBrightness 88.8/88.9/88.5 with meanR ranges of 7/5/4 counts; port 77.9/80.2/82.9 with meanR ranges of 19/28/43 counts. The brightness gap, the confetti ornaments and the block snow reproduce at every seed.

CONTROLS: --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' on BOTH sides and meta.json lists controls: [] for orig and port. Control surfaces match exactly; no dialed comparison is possible or needed. Neither side binds sensor globals (wantsSensors false on both, sensors 'off').
feedback: Draw each snowflake as ONE pixel, not a 2x2 block. The port's flakes snap to even coordinates (2-px horizontal runs start on an even column 422 times vs 69 odd; vertical pairs start on an even row 635 vs 152), so whatever computes the flake's cell is halving the resolution in both axes. The original's flake is 1 px tall and 1 px wide, spread across at most two adjacent COLUMNS only while it is mid-transit, with genuinely antialiased split values (e.g. 112/255 then 31/255) — never two rows, never two columns at full 255 simultaneously.

Cut flake lifetime by ~3x. Measured per-pixel dwell at 20 fps: original median 2.00 s / mean 1.87 s / max 4.5 s; port median 6.50 s / mean 5.92 s / max 14.0 s. Onset rates already agree (orig 5.77/s, port 4.98/s), so do not change spawn rate — shorten the fade/retire time until median dwell is ~2 s. That alone takes standing coverage from 29.5 px/frame back to the original's 10.8, and takes the port's meanR swing (52-101 over 240 s) back toward the original's tight 77-84.

Make flakes actually translate. The original's snow drifts rightward coherently at ~0.67-0.83 px/s (cross-correlation of the snow field peaks at lag +1 px at dt=1.2 s and +2 px at dt=3.0 s, with the -1 lag near zero). The port's correlation is pinned at lag 0 out to dt=3.0 s with a symmetric lag profile: its blocks light up in sequence rightward but never turn OFF behind, so one flake becomes a bar up to 14 px long instead of a moving point. Horizontal run-length distributions: orig {1:114, 2:110, 3:30, 4:3}, port {1:73, 2:85, 3:82, 4:49, 5:30, 6:26, 7:7, 8:17, 9:9, 11:4, 14:1}. Fixing the retire step fixes both the bars and the missing drift.

Restrict the ornament hues to red and blue. The original's saturated garlands live in exactly two hue zones — 359-20 deg (a 3-px ramp h9,15,20 on row7 and a 5-px ramp h359,4,9,14,19 on row14) and 240-261 deg (5-px ramps h241..261 on row9 and h240..261 on row16) — plus one stray green pixel at h138 and 26 px of low-saturation silver. The port cycles the full wheel: orange h12-36, green h107-127, azure h194-223, violet h285-305. Drop everything outside red/orange and blue.

Make the garlands long stripes, not 2-px dots. Original silver runs at 20x20 are 9 px (row8 cols5-13), 10 px (row13 cols7-16), 4 px (row12 cols3-6) and 3 px (row14 cols17-19), and its coloured runs are 3 and 5 px hue ramps. Every one of the port's saturated ornaments is a 2-px pair. Increase run length so the tree reads as banded tinsel rather than confetti.

Brighten the whole palette. Targets from exact t=0 dumps: sky [57,60,142] (port draws [26,44,89] — 0.54x brightness and hue 223 deg instead of 238 deg, so it needs to be both brighter and more indigo/less azure); ground and trunk [107,51,10] (port [63,34,12], correct hue, 0.59x brightness); silver tinsel [152,149,122] (port [127,116,89]). Whole-scene meanBrightness on the fixup rig is 88-91 on the original vs 71-82 on the port.

Shift the tree green ~11 degrees yellower: the original draws [40,203,0], which is exactly the sweep's signature Christmas green 51,255,0 scaled by 0.796 (hue 108 deg); the port draws [4,203,0] (hue 119 deg). Same value, wrong hue.
Shrink the star by one row and warm it slightly: original is 4 rows x 4 cols = 16 px on rows 2-5 at [255,235,61] (hue 53.7); port is 5 rows x 4 cols = 20 px on rows 2-6 at [255,215,76] (hue 46.6).

Snow COLOUR LOGIC is already right — do not rewrite it. Both sides correctly use two tones split by background (pale over sky, saturated over tree) and both fade flakes through dim values so they appear as dark specks. Only nudge the hues: orig sky tone [255,244,153] (hue 53.5) vs port [255,232,153] (46.5); orig tree tone [255,235,63] (hue 53.7, sat 0.75) vs port [255,194,38] (hue 43.1, sat 0.85).

Scene geometry needs no work at all: tree silhouette, star column, 3-row ground band and the rig-width mapping are already exact (grid 20x20 and strip 400 are byte-identical on both sides; grid 40x10 diverges from 20x20 by 161 px on the original and 159 on the port, i.e. the same width sensitivity).

Open question for a fix pass: the original errors with 'array index out of bounds' at frame 0 whenever pixelCount is not a multiple of 20 (verified failing at strip 64, working at strip 300 and grid 20x20); the port renders at any count. Decide whether the port should reproduce that constraint or keep its tolerance — the 20x20 fixup rig hides the difference entirely.
